event.detail: Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc. Drop or refuse retired container selections when using a stored setup, with an explanation. No path creates another old-style session.’ This patch preserves decoding and explicit removal rather than silently continuing old isolation. event.summary: Container launch progress loses the selected host name
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 350a4b33b6d4476f4a78e43cea124bc2b828f462. TLDR: While a new container is launching, its progress pill shows an internal host number (for example, ‘dev container on host 7’) instead of the container host name the user selected. Source: create_form.rs:6099-6102 constructs PendingLaunch using environment_ui::target_label(&target, &[]). environment_ui.rs:302-315 resolves Podman host names only from the places slice and otherwise falls back to format!("host {host}"). Passing an empty slice therefore guarantees that every container launch takes the fallback, although the same form already has environment_places and uses it for the visible placement label at create_form.rs:4395-4400. Contract: SPEC.md, Creation, says the pending pill names ‘the captured host's name and elapsed seconds’; Container sessions additionally says ‘The footer names the new container and its host.’ Preserve the selected place label in the accepted submission and pass it into PendingLaunch, rather than resolving against an empty catalog after the await. Suggested bucket: other (mislabelled progress without an established launch-target or data-loss consequence). Confidence: confirmed by source; no runtime execution. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none checked. Material caveat: the request still carries the correct LaunchTarget, and the main placement/footer label resolves through the actual catalog; this finding concerns the pending progress display only. Could-be-highest: no established route; merely seeing an internal numeric fallback does not establish wrong-target execution.

TLDR: A new container's pending launch pill can show its internal host number (for example, ‘dev container on host 7’) instead of the selected container host's name while waiting for admission or usable stage progress. Every container launch therefore captures the fallback despite the form having environment_places and using it at create_form.rs:4395-4400. launch_progress.rs:104-120 displays pending.host when stage is absent, and :144-145 reveals it after two seconds; api/sandbox_sessions.rs:67-104 awaits HTTP admission before publishing the host/run needed for stage observations. The request may wait on network/admission/configuration-save ordering, so this path does not require stage progress to be absent permanently. SPEC_impl.md, GUI: Dioxus, says ‘One component renders its captured host/name and elapsed time after two seconds.’ Capture the selected place label with the submission and pass that label into PendingLaunch. Confidence: confirmed source analysis; no runtime execution. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none checked. Material caveats: the request still carries the correct LaunchTarget, the main placement/footer label uses the real catalog, and launch_progress.rs:105-106 lets a later provisioning stage replace this generic label, limiting visible exposure to periods without stage progress. Original consequence retained: internal host number appears instead of selected name. Could-be-highest: no established route; a numeric fallback display does not establish wrong-target execution.

event.summary: Container launch progress loses the selected host name
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 350a4b33b6d4476f4a78e43cea124bc2b828f462; later-repair check through 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db. TLDR: If a new container launch waits at least two seconds without usable provisioning-stage progress, its generic progress pill names an internal host number instead of the selected container host's name. Original display consequence retained; this is not wrong-target execution. Proven path: create_form.rs:6097-6102 installs PendingLaunch with target_label(&target, &[]) before calling/awaiting create_environment_session (:6105 onward). environment_ui.rs:302-315 uses places to resolve a Podman host's name and necessarily falls back to ‘host {host}’ for an empty slice. PendingLaunch::new initializes stage=None (launch_progress.rs:56-65), label_parts uses host only when no stage (:104-120), and LaunchProgress waits two seconds (:144-145). pending_launch makes composer_hidden true (create_form.rs:3496-3497) and the hidden root explicitly mounts LaunchProgress (:7648-7656), so hidden presentation does not suppress the pill. Usable stage progress cannot precede admission: api/sandbox_sessions.rs:67-104 awaits HTTP response and validates host/run headers before setting sandbox_run; create_form.rs:3465-3483 polls only a known run, requires matching run id and a running step, then calls observe_stage. Before that, stage necessarily stays absent. The common send funnel awaits preceding configuration-save tickets before HTTP (api.rs:2488-2500) and then awaits the response (:2512-2517); helm sessions/sandbox.rs:61-84 also awaits start_session_environment admission before constructing response headers. Hence delayed configuration ordering, network or admission can expose the generic numeric label beyond two seconds; even after headers it remains until a successful matching running-step observation. No runtime frequency or timing claim is made. A later stage replaces the whole generic label (launch_progress.rs:105-106), so the fault need not remain visible throughout preparation. Contract: SPEC.md Creation requires ‘the captured host's name and elapsed seconds’; SPEC_impl.md GUI: Dioxus says ‘One component renders its captured host/name and elapsed time after two seconds.’ Fix by capturing target_label with the actual places snapshot before dispatch and storing it in PendingLaunch. Later repair check: at end revision create_form.rs:6073 still passes &[]; environment_ui.rs:452-464 retains numeric fallback; launch_progress.rs has no changes across the range. Suggested bucket: other; confidence: confirmed source/contract analysis, no reproduction or execution. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none established; caller identifies g077/f5 as distinct missing size presentation, and g060/l1/g061/l5 as status-refresh lifetime concerns. This record is solely generic numeric host naming; those issues are not required for its delayed-admission route. Could-be-highest: no established security/loss-of-work route. Request uses the captured correct LaunchTarget and the main placement label uses the real places list; do not infer wrong-target creation from this display bug. No unresolved premise remains.

event.detail: Reviewed commit: 350a4b33b6d4476f4a78e43cea124bc2b828f462. TLDR: Opening an environment launcher while fleet notices keep arriving more often than its recipe/settings read finishes can leave recipes and saved environment quick launches loading for the duration of that activity. Each notice cancels the unfinished read and starts it over instead of allowing an answer to land. Source route: create_form.rs:3237-3243 fetches recipes then Tensorlake settings sequentially in one Resource; the new :3245-3248 feed callback unconditionally restarts this resource, environment history and build status. Cargo.lock pins dioxus-hooks 0.7.10 (:1528-1531); its actual installed primary source src/use_resource.rs:29 initializes value=None, :46-66 sets Some(res) only after completion, and :191-194 Resource::restart cancels the current task then creates another. Restart retains an earlier completed value, but cannot supply one before the first completion. use_feed_reader in UI feed.rs:289-314 coalesces only notices already handled by one effect; it has no knowledge of these resource tasks and invokes the restart callback on each newly observed notice. Helm events.rs:239-248 forwards successive revisions without a read-duration gate. Thus if every delivered-notice gap is shorter than this two-request catalog lifetime, no task can reach value.set(Some(...)) until activity quiets. Normal notice producers and cadence are checked next; the confirmed scheduling consequence is conditional, not an observed frequency/timing claim. Readiness impact is concrete: :3257-3266 derives recipe names only from this result, initial template replay waits at :5331-5337, shortcut replay waits at :5402-5407, and actual environment submission requires the completed catalog at :5999-6024.
